answer_1.quote: In this paper, we study both explicit and implicit social biases by designing fairness-related questions and tasks that, while appearing to assist user requests, may reveal underlying biases.
answer_1.outputs: The generated outputs include answers to multiple-choice and yes-no questions, image descriptions, and form completions that are analyzed for social biases.

answer_2.quote: We compute the Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) to measure variations in the distribution of choices across different demographic groups.

answer_3.quote: Once the VLM responses are obtained, answers for each attribute are extracted and categorized into predefined choices using GPT-4o.
methods: categorization of responses into predefined choices

answer_4.quote: We employ human annotators to assess 370 attribute pairs, distributed across 19 questionnaires.
answer_4.guideline: Participants rate bias on a five-point scale, ranging from "(1) No Bias" to "(5) Severe Bias."
